title: British racing driver says he ‘owes his life’ to rival who rescued him from burning car after crash
content:
British racing driver Ollie Millroy said that he owes “his life” to rival driver Loek Hartog after the Dutchman rescued him from his burning car during a China GT Championship race on Saturday.

At the 20-minute mark into the GT3 race at the Shanghai International circuit, Neil Verhagen’s BMW and David Chen’s Ferrari came together towards the end of the track’s long back straight, with the pair losing control of their cars and sliding into the path of Millroy’s AAI Motorsports Ferrari, forcefully striking it from the side.

Millroy’s car burst into flames and spun into the barriers. Footage circulated on social media appears to show Hartog immediately stopping his car before pulling off part of the door on Millroy’s vehicle. He appears to then find a fire extinguisher to put out the flames, before pulling the 35-year-old from the car.

The race was red flagged and Millroy was later shown on the broadcast sat down against a barrier while being attended to by medical staff.

In a post on Instagram on Sunday, Millroy confirmed that he had suffered five broken ribs, alongside several other injuries. In the post, he shared an image of Hartog extinguishing the fire and thanked him for saving his life.

“I’m laying here tonight with five broken ribs, broken collar bone, broken hand and finger, and a bruised lung, but it could have been much worse.

“Thank you Loek. I owe you my life for your selfless act today.”

Hartog addressed the incident after the race on his Instagram story.

“When I saw a car turning into a huge fireball far ahead, there wasn’t really a decision to make,” he wrote. “From what I had seen, I genuinely believed the driver might not be able to get out by himself. I stopped, got out and went towards the car.”

“There was never a moment of doubt.

“It was scary. There were moments where I didn’t know I would actually be able to get Ollie out. But this isn’t about what I did, and I’m sure many people in the same position would have reacted exactly the same way.”
